name: Abnormal Origin of the Pulmonary Artery
aliases: Anomalous Origin of the Pulmonary Artery

criteria.description: Identification of anomalous origin of one pulmonary artery branch from the ascending aorta or other systemic artery on imaging
Presence of signs of pulmonary overcirculation or heart failure in infancy
Echocardiographic evidence of abnormal pulmonary artery origin and associated cardiac anomalies
Hemodynamic confirmation of abnormal pulmonary artery origin and pulmonary hypertension

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of anomalous pulmonary artery origin plus clinical signs consistent with pulmonary overcirculation or heart failure
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging modalities including echocardiography, CT angiography, or cardiac MRI.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Differential cyanosis with upper body saturation higher than lower body
searchTerms: blue color difference between upper and lower body

pathognomonic.symptomName: Continuous cardiac murmur due to pulmonary artery shunting
searchTerms: continuous heart murmur from artery shunt
heart murmur due to blood flow between vessels
constant murmur from pulmonary artery connection

pathognomonic.symptomName: Early onset congestive heart failure symptoms in neonates
searchTerms: early heart failure signs in newborns
fast breathing due to excess lung blood flow
failure to gain weight as baby

common.symptomName: Hepatomegaly secondary to right heart strain
searchTerms: enlarged liver from right heart strain
liver swelling due to heart problems

occasional.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension symptoms such as exertional dyspnea
searchTerms: exertional shortness of breath due to lung pressure
heart rhythm problems from cardiac strain

occasional.symptomName: Chest pain due to myocardial ischemia
searchTerms: chest pain from reduced heart blood flow
coughing up blood from lung vessels
hemoptysis due to lung vessel issues
nerve issues from lack of oxygen

rare.symptomName: Endocarditis due to abnormal flow patterns
searchTerms: heart infection from abnormal blood flow
infection of heart lining due to flow issues

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) indicating cardiac strain
Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia in some cases
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating anomalous pulmonary artery origin
CT angiography or cardiac MRI confirming pulmonary artery anatomy
Cardiac catheterization showing abnormal pulmonary artery pressures
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with congenital heart disease syndromes
other: Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings

distinguishingFeatures: Patent ductus arteriosus presents with continuous murmur but normal pulmonary artery origin
No anomalous pulmonary artery origin on imaging
Absent or atretic pulmonary valve with no antegrade flow

redFlags: Severe congestive heart failure in neonate
references: Graham TP Jr, et al. Anomalous origin of the pulmonary artery: clinical and surgical considerations. Circulation. 1974.
Anderson RH, et al. Pediatric Cardiology and Pulmonary Artery Anomalies. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases. 2010.
Mavroudis C, Backer CL. Surgical management of anomalous origin of the pulmonary artery. Seminars in Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery. 2000.
